result.text: Title: Building a custom machine out of Lego bricks When building a custom machine out of Lego bricks, you first need to develop the basic design.
After that, you order certain Lego brick sets.
You give the lego sets to a group of children which should sort the parts for you (into a number of containers).
Your machine is built out of a number of subcomponents.
You build them individually, using parts from the sorted containers.
If there are no more parts in a container, you reorder individual parts.
After building each subcomponent, you have to test them individually and (if each test is successful) assemble them.
If subcomponents are not tested successfully, you have to redesign and rebuild them.

result.rule: When the description identifies a specific trigger, decision criterion, or performed activity: Use a concise BPMN label that expresses that meaning; do not substitute a related event, outcome, or different decision.

When the description states a specific activity or process-ending outcome: Label the corresponding BPMN activity or end event with a concise phrase that preserves the stated action or outcome; do not substitute a related action or add an unsupported one.

When the description explicitly identifies an action or process milestone at a point in the flow: Label the corresponding BPMN task with that stated action or milestone; do not substitute a related action or label only a constituent activity when the description identifies the broader milestone.

When the description states an activity with explicit alternatives or qualifiers that distinguish its scope: Label the corresponding BPMN element concisely while preserving those stated distinctions; do not generalize them away.
